info.title: VFS Link File Server API
info.description: HTTP API for browsing and operating on VFS Link files, uploads, shares, thumbnails, and storage-key drift. Deployments may enable HTTP Basic authentication for the entire service.

get.summary: Get storage status and aggregate statistics
List direct children of a directory

post.description: Small operations complete synchronously with 200. Large directory operations can be queued and return 202; poll the operation URL from the Location header.
Small operations complete synchronously with 200. Large directory operations can be queued and return 202.

200.description: Current operation state. Terminal statuses are completed or failed.

post.summary: Move files or directories to trash
post.description: Small operations complete synchronously with 200. Large directory operations can be queued and return 202.
Small operations complete synchronously with 200. Large directory operations can be queued and return 202.
At least one trash ID is required. The deletion may return synchronously or as an asynchronous operation.
The deletion may return synchronously or as an asynchronous operation.

get.summary: List the directory tree one level deep

200.description: Directory node and its direct child directories

parameters.name: disposition
parameters.description: Use inline to request browser display; every other value uses attachment.

200.description: Raw file bytes. Content-Type is inferred from the file extension and Content-Disposition includes the filename.

post.description: Checks up to 1000 logical paths before content upload begins. No content checksum is calculated. Keep each opaque targetVersion and send it when creating an overwrite session; a changed target is rejected with UPLOAD_TARGET_CHANGED before an upload capability is allocated.

200.description: Path availability and target snapshots in request order

post.description: For local storage, uploadUrl points to this API's content endpoint. For GCS it is an opaque resumable session URI. Send each chunk with a client-generated Content-Range in addition to the fixed headers in the response. overwrite=true requires the targetVersion returned by upload preflight; stale versions return UPLOAD_TARGET_CHANGED before a session is created.

201.description: Upload session created, including its upload capability

get.description: Returns the storage-confirmed uploadedSize and repeats the protected upload capability for active sessions so an authenticated same-origin client can resume after reload. Expired sessions have status=expired and empty capability fields.

put.summary: Upload content through the file server
put.description: Used by local upload sessions. Send Content-Range: bytes start-end/total. start must equal uploadedSize from the latest status response. Incomplete chunks return 308 with a Range header describing committed bytes; the final chunk returns 200. GCS sessions use the same headers directly against their opaque uploadUrl.

200.description: Final chunk accepted by the upload session

308.description: Chunk committed; send the next chunk after the byte identified by Range

Range.description: Contiguous committed byte range, omitted when uploadedSize is zero

post.summary: Complete and commit an upload session
post.description: Call this after bytes have been uploaded either through the local content endpoint or directly to GCS.

post.summary: Attach a WebP thumbnail to archive files
post.description: The thumbnail must be a non-empty WebP no larger than 2 MiB. Width and height must each be between 1 and 512. paths is a JSON-encoded array in a multipart text field.

get.description: This endpoint remains readable when drift mutation is disabled or unavailable. With refresh=true it performs a storage scan; otherwise it reads the current snapshot. An unavailable or missing snapshot is represented by a 200 response with available=false or snapshotStatus=missing.

post.summary: Start or join the current asynchronous drift rescan
post.description: Starts one server-owned read-only rescan. If a pending or running job already exists, the same job is returned instead of starting a duplicate. The job survives browser disconnects and can be resumed after an expired lease.

202.description: The new or existing rescan job was accepted

get.summary: Get and, when necessary, resume the current drift rescan
get.description: Returns the singleton rescan job on every device. Reading a pending or expired running job can kick background processing. A completed or failed job remains current until the next manual rescan starts.

200.description: Current rescan state, or null before the first rescan

post.description: Mutation must be explicitly enabled, the storage driver must be GCS, and the metadata/object stores must support drift state. No storage object is changed by plan creation.

201.description: Immutable repair plan created from the current snapshot

get.description: Returns completed, failed, pending, and running actions that have not been globally dismissed. Results use a stable createdAt and id descending order. Use limit and offset for bounded pages, or all=true for a single complete snapshot. all=true is mutually exclusive with limit and offset.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: When true, returns all visible actions in one response and must not be combined with limit or offset.

post.summary: Start an asynchronous drift repair action
post.description: Mutation must be explicitly enabled and use GCS. The idempotency key is optional; if omitted the server generates a UUID. The accepted action runs asynchronously and must be polled to a terminal completed or failed status.

get.summary: Get and, when necessary, resume a drift repair action
get.description: Reading a pending or expired running action can kick its background processing. Failed actions remain terminal until an explicit retry POST. Poll until status is completed or failed.

delete.summary: Globally dismiss a terminal drift repair action
delete.description: Soft-dismisses a completed or failed action from action lists on every device. The action record remains available by id. Repeated dismissal is idempotent.

basicAuth.description: Enabled only when the deployment configures Basic authentication credentials.

PathQuery.name: path
PathQuery.description: Normalized logical path relative to the VFS root. Empty means root.

RequiredPathQuery.name: path
RequiredPathQuery.description: Logical file path relative to the VFS root.

Unauthorized.description: Basic authentication is enabled and credentials are missing or invalid

Conflict.description: Request conflicts with the current resource or session state

NotImplemented.description: The configured storage or metadata backend does not support this capability

AcceptedOperation.description: File operation accepted for asynchronous execution

Location.description: Relative URL to poll for the operation state

LogicalPath.description: Slash-separated logical path relative to the root, without a leading slash.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code for structured errors such as UPLOAD_TARGET_CHANGED.

name.description: New basename, not a full path.

targetVersion.description: Opaque snapshot returned by upload preflight. Required when overwrite is true.
Opaque target snapshot. Clients must not inspect or construct it.

uploadedSize.description: Contiguous byte count confirmed by local staging or the GCS resumable session.

uploadUrl.description: Relative local API URL or absolute opaque GCS session URI. Empty for complete or expired sessions.

headers.description: Fixed headers such as Content-Type. The client adds Content-Range for every chunk.

status.description: Snapshot status or planned for a plan item.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional caller key. The server generates a UUID when omitted or blank.
